interest: This file provides valuable historical insight into the legal, financial, and diplomatic complexities of unwinding international banking networks and wartime asset freezes following World War II. It illustrates how the U.S. Office of Alien Property and the New York State Banking Department collaborated with the Department of State to protect vested surplus assets against private claims by coordinating cross-border investigations in Allied-occupied Japan and Nationalist China. In particular, the records shed light on the prewar trade in strategic commodities (lubricating oil) just prior to the Pacific War, the shadowy financial operations of Japanese-sponsored puppet banks such as the Hua Hsing Commercial Bank in occupied Shanghai, and the difficult procedures foreign private businesses in Southeast Asia faced when seeking restitution for funds entangled in Japanese bank liquidations before formal peace treaties and claims tribunals were established.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.51611) documents diplomatic and legal inquiries from February 1946 through July 1947 concerning the postwar liquidation of U.S. branch agencies of Japanese banks—specifically the New York branches of the Sumitomo Bank, Ltd. and the Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd.—under the supervision of the New York State Banking Department and the U.S. Office of Alien Property. The documentation centers on two primary claims arising from pre-Pearl Harbor commercial transactions frozen by wartime economic controls: first, efforts by the Royal Siamese Embassy and the American Legation in Bangkok to trace and recover $6,455 in frozen credits belonging to the Pisal Panite Trading Company, which were routed in 1941 through the Banca Commerciale Italiana in Turin and Sumitomo Bank branches in New York and Osaka; and second, federal and New York state efforts to defend against a $60,387.73 recovery claim brought by American merchant Neil C. Potter (Neil C. Potter v. The Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd.) concerning an uncompleted prewar export of lubricating oil to Japanese firm Maruzen Sekiyu Kabushiki Kaisha financed by the Japanese puppet Hua Hsing Commercial Bank in Shanghai. Through diplomatic correspondence between Washington, Nanking, Bangkok, and Tokyo, the file details the complex jurisdictional, accounting, and legal obstacles encountered when untangling international commercial transactions across Axis, occupied, and Allied jurisdictions in the immediate aftermath of World War II.

subfiles.about: Records the internal routing of file 894.51611 to the Division of Southeast Asian Affairs in connection with airgram A-24 to Bangkok.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State charge slip recording that decimal file 894.51611 was charged to the Division of Southeast Asian Affairs (SEA) on April 16, 1946. It notes an enclosure dated February 15, 1946, and contains the remark 'A 24 apr 15 to Bangkok'.
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip for File 894.51611

subfiles.about: Instructs the American Legation in Bangkok to seek further account details from Pisal Panite Trading Company regarding its frozen funds in the Sumitomo Bank.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State James F. Byrnes transmits Airgram No. A-24 to the American Legation in Bangkok regarding the frozen dollar account of the Pisal Panite Trading Company. The Alien Property Custodian advised that the New York Superintendent of Banks, supervising the liquidation of Sumitomo Bank, Ltd., found no record of the Siamese firm in the bank's books, though it may have been recorded under Banca Commerciale Italiana of Turin. The Legation is instructed to obtain additional information from the firm, such as account opening dates and alternate names, to facilitate claim disposition.
subfiles.title: Airgram No. A-24 to American Legation, Bangkok, regarding Pisal Panite Trading Company account

subfiles.about: Transmits an inquiry from the Siamese Ministry of Foreign Affairs concerning a $6,455 frozen account of Pisal Panite Trading Company in Sumitomo Bank, New York.
keywords: Bank of Asia for Industry and Commerce
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Charles E. Brookhart reports on a communication from the Siamese Ministry of Foreign Affairs regarding a $6,455 credit balance frozen in the New York branch of Sumitomo Bank, Ltd. The account belonged to the Pisal Panite Trading Company (spelled Fisal Panite Trading Company) and had been remitted in 1941 from Banca Commerciale Italiana in Turin by order of the Bank of Asia for Industry and Commerce in Bangkok. Brookhart requests a report from the Department of State on the status of the funds to assist the Siamese ministry.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 49 from American Legation, Bangkok, on frozen account of Siamese firm in Sumitomo Bank

subfiles.about: Requests diplomatic assistance in China to investigate records of Hua Hsing Commercial Bank and Yokohama Specie Bank concerning a $60,387.73 claim by Neil C. Potter.
subfiles.summary: Philip Blacklow of the Office of Alien Property requests the Department of State to initiate an investigation through diplomatic channels in China regarding Neil C. Potter v. The Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd. Potter sued the New York agency for $60,387.73 for 2,376 barrels of lubricating oil allegedly delivered at Manila under a modified letter of credit originally opened by Hua Hsing Commercial Bank of Shanghai for Maruzen Sekiyu Kabushiki Kaisha. Blacklow explains that defeating the claim would increase surplus proceeds vested by the U.S. Government under Vesting Order No. 915 and sets forth specific factual questions regarding the security deposits, letter of credit modifications, and payment arrangements.
subfiles.title: Letter from Philip Blacklow to Walter S. Surrey regarding Neil C. Potter v. The Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd.

subfiles.about: Confirms cable negotiations and debits for lubricating oil shipments under Hua Hsing Commercial Bank Letter of Credit #14.
subfiles.summary: The New York Agency of Yokohama Specie Bank confirms to its Shanghai branch the cable negotiation of $151,896.10 under Hua Hsing Commercial Bank Letter of Credit #14 in favor of Neil C. Potter. The letter encloses shipping receipts, invoices, and bills of lading for 7,603 barrels of lubricating oil shipped from New Orleans to Shanghai aboard the S/S Zoella Lykes. It confirms debiting Shanghai's account for the negotiated funds and cable expenses, and requests remittance of a 1/16% commission.
subfiles.title: Enclosure: Letter from Yokohama Specie Bank, New York, to Shanghai Branch regarding Potter Letter of Credit

subfiles.about: Transmits the Office of Alien Property's request to Nanking for an investigation in China into the Neil C. Potter claim against Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the American Mission in Nanking a copy of Philip Blacklow's letter of January 21, 1947, regarding the Neil C. Potter claim against the New York agency of Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd. The Mission is instructed to conduct an appropriate investigation in China to secure the required banking information and records. The findings are to be forwarded to the Department of State for transmittal to the Department of Justice.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 248 to American Mission, Nanking, regarding Yokohama Specie Bank investigation
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge of the American Mission, Nanking

subfiles.about: Informs the Office of Alien Property that its investigation request has been forwarded to the American Embassy in Nanking.
subfiles.summary: Walter S. Surrey acknowledges receipt of Philip Blacklow's letter of January 21, 1947, concerning Vesting Order No. 915 and the liquidation of Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd. (New York). He informs Blacklow that the request has been dispatched to the American Embassy at Nanking with instructions to conduct an investigation into the transactions. Surrey notes that the findings will be communicated to the Office of Alien Property as soon as they are received.
subfiles.title: Letter from Walter S. Surrey to Philip Blacklow regarding transmittal of inquiry to Nanking

subfiles.about: Requests the Political Adviser in Tokyo to check whether records of Sumitomo Bank in Osaka reflect a $6,455 credit for Pisal Panite Trading Company.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State George C. Marshall requests the U.S. Political Adviser to SCAP in Tokyo to investigate whether the records of Sumitomo Bank, Osaka, indicate a credit of $6,455 in favor of the Pisal Panite Trading Company of Bangkok. The instruction summarizes data from the Siamese Embassy and the New York State Banking Department Liquidation Bureau indicating the funds were wired in February 1941 from Banca Commerciale Italiana via New York to Sumitomo Bank in Osaka. It notes that while private funds cannot currently be transferred out of Japan, obtaining these facts will assist the Siamese Government in advising the claimant on future restitution procedures.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 519 to U.S. Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo, regarding Pisal Panite Trading Company account
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Requests assistance and clarification from the Department of State regarding Pisal Panite Trading Company's claim of $6,455 against Sumitomo Bank.
subfiles.summary: Prince Wan Waithayakon, Ambassador of Siam, solicits the assistance of Abbot L. Moffat regarding the $6,455 claim of the Pisal Panite Trading Company against Sumitomo Bank. He recounts that the funds were sent from Banca Commerciale Italiana in Turin to Sumitomo Bank, New York, in early 1941, but Japanese foreign exchange regulations and the outbreak of war prevented transfer to Japan. Inquiries made through Muller, Maclean & Co. with the New York Banking Department suggested the funds were cabled to Osaka, and the Ambassador asks for clarification on the funds' whereabouts, claim formalities, and the prospects of recovery.
subfiles.title: Letter No. 867/2490 from Prince Wan Waithayakon to Abbot L. Moffat regarding Pisal Panite Trading Company claim

subfiles.about: Informs the Siamese Ambassador that the U.S. Mission in Tokyo has been instructed to inspect Sumitomo Bank records in Osaka regarding Pisal Panite Trading Company.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Prince Wan Waithayakon's letter of May 27 concerning the account of Pisal Panite Trading Company with Sumitomo Bank. The note informs the Ambassador that the Department of State has requested its representatives in Tokyo to ascertain whether the account appears in the records of Sumitomo Bank at Osaka. It cautions, however, that even if the funds are identified in Japan, no mechanism currently exists for private foreign claims against Japanese businesses to be presented for payment.
subfiles.title: Diplomatic Note from Secretary of State to Siamese Ambassador regarding Sumitomo Bank account

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Prince Wan Waithayakon's letter of May 27, 1947, during Abbot L. Moffat's absence from the Department of State.
subfiles.summary: Kenneth P. Landon, writing on behalf of Abbot L. Moffat during his absence, sends an interim reply to Siamese Ambassador Prince Wan Waithayakon regarding the credit balance of Pisal Panite Trading Company with Sumitomo Bank, Ltd., New York. Landon acknowledges the Ambassador's letter of May 27 and notes that the matter has been referred to appropriate officials. He assures the Ambassador that a further substantive reply will be provided as soon as possible.
subfiles.title: Letter from Kenneth P. Landon to Prince Wan Waithayakon regarding Pisal Panite Trading Company

subfiles.about: Transmits the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs' findings regarding the Neil C. Potter claim and Hua Hsing Commercial Bank records.
subfiles.summary: First Secretary of Embassy William T. Turner forwards a translation of a note from the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs concerning the Neil C. Potter claim of $60,387.73 against Yokohama Specie Bank. The Embassy reports that investigations conducted through the Ministry of Finance, the Bank of China, and the Central Bank of China's liquidation office found no record of the transaction in Hua Hsing Commercial Bank books or takeover accounts. Turner adds that because the puppet bank conducted all non-Japanese foreign exchange through Yokohama Specie Bank, further records are unlikely to be found, though the Embassy requested a re-check.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 891 from American Embassy, Nanking, on claim against Yokohama Specie Bank

subfiles.about: Reports the findings of Chinese banking and liquidation authorities regarding Hua Hsing Commercial Bank and Yokohama Specie Bank records on Neil C. Potter.
subfiles.from: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Republic of China)
subfiles.summary: The Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs informs the American Embassy in Nanking of results from inquiries conducted by the Ministry of Finance regarding the 1941 letter of credit issued for Neil C. Potter and Maruzen Sekiyu Kabushiki Kaisha. The Bank of China reported no entry in the guaranteed liabilities taken over from Yokohama Specie Bank in Shanghai, and the Central Bank of China reported that old Hua Hsing Commercial Bank records have not yet been checked and handed over. Former staff of the puppet bank stated that all international remittances outside Japan were routed through Yokohama Specie Bank and suggested that Potter negotiate directly with Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.title: Enclosure to Despatch 891: Note No. Tung-36/14458 from Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs
